data.title: The business case for asset finance
data.text:
Working across the market also gives finance providers a broader understanding of common customer priorities, from fuel efficiency to total cost of ownership. This helps them tailor finance solutions for partners. Finance can be structured around the asset, whether new, used, or retrofitted, and aligned with the customer's cash flow.

For cement equipment suppliers and OEMs, finance should not replace the technical sales conversation. But when finance is introduced at the right stage, it can help customers assess affordability alongside performance and long-term value. In a market where investment decisions are under pressure, specialist, integrated finance can make the difference between interest and commitment.

Learn more about Vendor Finance at Siemens Financial Services here .

Read the article online at: https://www.worldcement.com/special-reports/24092026/the-business-case-for-asset-finance/

data.title: The business case for asset finance
data.text:
Save to read list Published by Charlotte Sweby ,
                                        Editorial Assistant World Cement , Thursday, 24 September 2026 09:13

John Bolton, Siemens Financial Services UK, explains how making finance part of the sales process can strengthen the business case for both cement producers and customers themselves.

Cement producers are under pressure to invest in more efficient, productive, and resilient plants, but high capital costs can make investment decisions difficult. For equipment suppliers and OEMs, that creates a challenge. Even when the business case for new equipment is strong, customers may hesitate if the purchase places too much pressure on cash flow.

Finance can help bridge that gap. Yet it is often introduced only after equipment has been specified, priced, and selected. Bringing finance into the sales conversation earlier can make investment easier for customers, while helping suppliers support stronger, more confident buying decisions.

data.title: Anyang Indorama Gases secures ¥2.4 million for fertilizer capacity expansion
data.text: Anyang Indorama Gases Co., Ltd, a wholly owned subsidiary of Indorama Corporation Pte. Ltd, Singapore, has signed a &yen;2.4 billion (US$358 million) long-term loan facility with a consortium of five leading banks in China to finance its Phase II fertilizer capacity expansion project in Anyang City, Henan Province, China. The financing represents an important milestone in Indorama's brownfield expansion in China following its acquisition of the Anyang nitrogen fertilizer business earlier in 2026 and reinforces the Group's commitment to building competitive, cleaner, and more efficient fertilizer capacity. This expansion project is expected to double the company's urea fertilizers capacity (starting from syngas and ammonia) to approximately 2 million tpy by 2029. It will further strengthen the reliability of domestic fertilizer supply contributing to increasing food security, with more energy-efficient production processes across the site.This long-term financing was provided by OCBC Bank Ltd, Bank of China Ltd, Bank of Communications Co., Ltd, Bangkok Bank (China) Company Ltd and China CITIC Bank Co., Ltd. OCBC Bank Ltd acted as Coordinator and Facility Agent
